item.description:
Kento Alpha 0.9.20, build 2606

Paint

  • A new node, Paint (under Draw), made for cleanup: brush, eraser, clone, reveal, heal, dust, wire removal, blur, sharpen, smear, dodge and burn, from a tool rail over the picture.
  • The strip over the Viewer holds the brush (size, hardness, opacity, color), where clone takes from, the stroke's lifetime and the channels. Click the tool chip for presets, each drawn on your own plate. Hold the right button for the marking menu.
  • Clone from Paint's own painted output on another frame. Onion skin (O) and split compare (Caps Lock) line a clone up. Auto grade matches the source's brightness to where it lands, and warp pins bend the source to fit.
  • Grain-aware strokes put the plate's own grain back under what you paint, so a clone doesn't leave a smooth patch.
  • Every stroke stays editable: pick one in History and the same strip edits it, in blue-gray, until Done. Drag strokes to reorder them, Delete takes one out.
  • Painted frames are cached as tiles where there's paint, in memory and then on the local disk, so playing and cloning across frames are quick.
  • Edit brush... opens the brush editor: a live pad on your plate, shape, the pressure curve, tilt and speed, the stabilizer, blend modes including pigment mixing.
  • AI fill: paint over what to remove on a hero frame and Saku fills it, shown with its price first. It comes back as a reveal source for the frames around it, regrained.
  • Window > Workspaces > Paint: the Viewer large, History beside it.

AI roto: Isolate

  • A new node, Isolate (under Draw): click on an object in the Viewer and SAM 2 follows it through the shot, each object ending as a matte channel of its own (isolate.<name>). Alt-click takes away, a drag draws a box round it, and stroke lays points along a line for something thin.
  • Track both ways runs in the background while you work. The strip under the Viewer shows each frame green, amber or red by how sure the tracker is, lost frames hatched, so you can see where to click again.
  • Find every picks objects by name: type "cars" or "people, bikes" and each one SAM 3.1 finds on the frame becomes an object of its own, ready to track.
  • Edge: snap the matte's edge to the picture, decontaminate the edge's color, reduce chatter between frames, and add motion blur along the object's motion.
  • Out: a channel per object or Cryptomatte, alpha from every object, and Bake to EXR. The mattes are kept beside the comp, so it renders anywhere, the farm included, without the tracker.
  • Set up in Settings > Performance > AI roto: Find fills in what's on your Mac.

Saku, built in

  • Kento now ships its own Saku, the version Kento was made with, so Generate, Inpaint and AI fill work without installing anything first.
  • Settings > Generative > Provider keys: paste your Gemini, OpenAI, Replicate, fal, Higgsfield, Topaz and BytePlus keys there. Each is shown only by its last four characters and kept in Saku's own file, readable only by you.

Node Graph

  • Tidy lays the selection out as you would: each input straight above its port (a side input above and out to its side), rows evenly spaced, nothing overlapping, the bottom node kept where it is.
  • Zoomed out, the ports a hover reveals get room of their own outside the node, their labels level.

Faster

  • The Viewer's Visible difference compare is much faster on 4K pictures.

Remote control

  • Isolate and Paint are reachable too: Isolate's objects, prompts, Find every, Track and Bake; Paint's strokes, presets, cache and AI fill. 166 commands.

Kento Alpha 0.9.19, build 2586

3D

  • WriteGeo writes OBJ: the meshes in world space, laid out as Nuke writes them. Put #### in the file name to write a file for each frame.
  • An Axis can read its movement from an Alembic file: Read file keys it from the file's first axis, or the one you choose in axis in file.

Keying

  • LightKey's inside and outside masks work: the inside mask fills in the matte (with the inside replace colour), the outside mask cuts it away, from the mask's alpha or luminance.
  • LightKey's source crops work: Colour, Repeat, Reflect or Wrap outside the crop, before keying.
  • Fixed: LightKey's mask and background inputs were read in the wrong order from Nuke scripts. They now match Nuke: input 1 the inside mask, 2 the outside mask, 3 the background.

Deep

  • DeepSample lists the samples at its position in its panel, each one's front, back and channels, or with accumulate the running composite.
  • DeepReformat's black_outside and pbb work as in Nuke.

Other

  • VectorRetime's retimedChannels works: the channels you leave out pass through untouched instead of being retimed.

Kento Alpha 0.9.18, build 2571

Viewer

  • A new compare, Visible difference: how much someone would notice B differ from A, as a heatmap, black where they look the same through purple and orange to yellow where the difference is plain. It uses FLIP, NVIDIA's measure, on the linear pictures over the exposures that matter, so it plays down changes the eye wouldn't catch and plays up the ones it would. A few seconds an HD frame.
  • The same as a node, Visible Difference under Merge, with a choice of looking at the pictures as displayed, how far away you sit, and the plain error in place of the heatmap; its mean error is in its metadata.

Faster

  • Slow results the Viewer and renders work out (a big defocus, a denoise) are kept on disk in the cache folder and read back instead of being worked out again, after a long session or the next time you open the comp. Anything that changes a result, including a file it reads being rewritten, makes it a new one, so you never see an old picture. Turn it off with keep slow render results here for later sessions in Settings > Performance > Disk cache; Clear the cache empties them.
  • Renders from the command line keep them too (--no-disk-cache to skip it), so rendering a comp again skips what it worked out before.

Nodes

  • OCIOCDLTransform reads its grade from a .cc, .ccc or .cdl file: choose the file and its correction fills slope, offset, power and saturation; cccid is a menu of the file's corrections; Reload reads it again. read from file dims the grade, as in Nuke.
  • GenerateLUT writes .cms, .cub and .blut too, as Nuke does.
  • ChromaKeyer's insideMask works: on source alpha the input's alpha is added to the matte.
  • Encryptomatte's Export Write makes a Write beside it that writes every channel to a 32-bit EXR.
  • Card3D draws a card that crosses behind the camera: the part in front is drawn, its perspective running off toward the horizon, where before nothing was drawn.
  • ReConverge reads the disparity at convergepoint, so that point lands on the screen, as in Nuke.
  • SphericalTransform2's From-To and Look rotation modes turn the picture on a lat-long, where before they left it as it was.
  • A dimmed text field in Properties now looks dimmed.
